title: Titanium Intramedullary Nail
function: Tibial/femoral intramedullary nail with locking holes
alloyReason: ASTM F136 Ti-6Al-4V ELI is specified for this trauma fixation implant-grade component where controlled interstitials deliver high fatigue strength (>600 MPa @10^7 cyc) and corrosion resistance for permanent implantable devices. This rationale is driven by tibial/femoral intramedullary nail with locking holes and fat life requirements.
process: CNC swiss turning for trauma fixation geometry
Ultrasonic clean Class 10k for net-shape tolerance
surfaceTreatment: Electropolishing + passivation per ASTM F86 (20-30% HNO3, 30min @50C) achieving Ra <0.2um for implant-grade finish — tailored for tibialfemoral intramedullary nail application
commonFailures: Fatigue fracture at thread root under cyclic bending - resolved by thread rolling (not cutting) for compressive stress — critical for tibialfemoral intramedullary nail performance

faq.q: What specific material properties make Titanium Intramedullary Nail suitable for Tibial/femoral intramedullary nail with locking holes?
faq.a: Titanium Intramedullary Nail uses Ti-6Al-4V ELI because its yield strength, fatigue endurance, and corrosion resistance directly address trauma fixation operational demands. The alloy's specific strength enables mass reduction without section compromise, while the TiO2 passivation ensures long-term environmental resistance.

faq.q: What are the critical dimensional tolerances for Titanium Intramedullary Nail?
faq.a: Standard machining tolerance for Titanium Intramedullary Nail is +/-0.05mm (ISO 2768-m). Functional mating surfaces are held to +/-0.025mm with Ra 0.8um finish, verified specifically for tibialfemoral intramedullary nail requirements. Threaded features conform to ISO 965-2 Class 6g, verified with calibrated Go/No-Go ring gauges on 100% of production.

faq.q: Does Titanium Intramedullary Nail require any post-machining surface treatment?
faq.a: Yes. tibialfemoral intramedullary nail components require Electropolishing + passivation per ASTM F86 (20-30% HNO3, 30min @50C) achieving Ra <0.2um for implant-grade finish — tailored for tibialfemoral intramedullary nail application. This restores the natural TiO2 passive layer removed during machining and provides the required surface properties for the specific service environment. Key parameters include surface finish Ra 0.8um and passive layer thickness verification per applicable standards.

faq.q: What quality documentation is included with Titanium Intramedullary Nail shipments?
faq.a: Each shipment of Titanium Intramedullary Nail includes: (1) EN 10204 Type 3.1 MTR with full chemical analysis and mechanical properties; (2) Certificate of Conformance confirming all processes meet tibialfemoral intramedullary nail specifications; (3) Dimensional inspection report with actual vs nominal measurements on critical features; (4) Surface roughness certification per applicable standards. FAIR available on request.

faq.q: What is the MOQ and typical lead time for IM nail / Intramedullary rod trauma fixation components?
faq.a: Standard MOQ: 1 unit for prototype evaluation. Production lead time: 15-25 business days depending on quantity. Rush orders (3-5 days) available. Contact our supply chain team for volume-based tiered pricing.
